answer: On this worktree the corpus axes are MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD (canonical BSD-3-Clause), GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0, CC-BY (CC-BY-4.0), CC-BY-SA (CC-BY-SA-4.0), CC0 (CC0-1.0), unlicensed, and vendor-riders. Unlicensed is ALL-RIGHTS-RESERVED: 17 USC §106 keeps exclusive reproduction and distribution rights with the owner, so every unlicensed cell is FORBIDDEN (never permissive-by-default). Vendor riders are FORBIDDEN for a marketplace SKU; the live n8n Sustainable Use License grants distribution only free of charge for non-commercial purposes and grants no other rights. Permissive pairs (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, CC0, CC-BY) are TOGETHER with per-file notices. Software copyleft may share a SKU with those permissive licences (combined-work outbound GPL-3.0/AGPL-3.0, or GPL §5 aggregate if the works stay independent). GPL-3.0+AGPL-3.0 is TOGETHER via both licences' §13. MPL-2.0+GPL/AGPL is TOGETHER via MPL §3.3 Secondary License (no Exhibit B). CC-BY-SA versus GPL-3.0/AGPL-3.0/MPL-2.0 is SEPARATE-PACKAGE: CC-BY-SA-4.0 §3(b) share-alike is a different family; CC/FSF one-way compatibility to GPLv3 is a conversion path, not a mixed-licence SKU. packaging_model: A marketplace package is one downloadable SKU of independent workflows, skills or prompts, each retaining its licence and notices. This is not the IMP-0157 fusion lattice (which forbids producing a single fused body). GPL §5 aggregate is available when works stay separate and independent; if they form a larger program, copyleft §5(c) covers the whole. Cross-family share-alike is not treated as a mere aggregate for a single product SKU.
